To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) IBS is a multifactorial disorder; 2) the intestinal microbiota plays a role in the pathophysiology of IBS; 3) the intestinal microbiome may be modulated to treat IBS.

IBS is a functional gastrointestinal disorders that predominantly affects women; that its pathophysiology is multifactorial; that intestinal dysbiosis is one of the factors involved; that PI-IBS can put light on its mechanisms; that the comprehension of the interaction of the dysbiotic intestinal microbiota with the host will probably result in new treatments; that probiotics and antibiotics are two of the approaches that can be used for treating IBS.
IBS is a multifactorial syndrome, in which intestinal dysbiosis plays an important role.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathophysiological mechanisms of IBS and the development of targeted therapies.
the study of the intestinal microbiome, the role of the microbiome in health and disease, and the development of novel therapeutic interventions based on microbiome modulation.
a better understanding of the pathophysiology of IBS and the development of new treatment strategies.
